- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early/medium horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% based on sentiment decay.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true prices.
- In high-sentiment environments (e.g., >0.8), model often overconfidently predicts continuation; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the period; apply linear decay correction: subtract 1–2% per day from forecast starting day 5.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to pivot; force a 2–5 day mean reversion correction toward historical 14-day average.
